The `re.split()` call splits the string on every whitespace character **and keeps the whitespace itself** in the resulting list because the pattern contains a capturing group `(\s)`.

Running your snippet prints:

```python
['Hello,', ' ', 'world.', ' ', 'This,', ' ', 'is', ' ', 'a', ' ', 'test.', '']
```

Explanation of the output:

| Index | Element | Reason |
|-------|---------|--------|
| 0 | `'Hello,'` | Text before the first space |
| 1 | `' '` | The captured space after `"Hello,"` |
| 2 | `'world.'` | Text between the first and second spaces |
| 3 | `' '` | The captured space after `"world."` |
| 4 | `'This,'` | Text between the second and third spaces |
| 5 | `' '` | The captured space after `"This,"` |
| 6 | `'is'` | Text between the third and fourth spaces |
| 7 | `' '` | The captured space after `"is"` |
| 8 | `'a'` | Text between the fourth and fifth spaces |
| 9 | `' '` | The captured space after `"a"` |
| 10 | `'test.'` | Text after the last space |
| 11 | `''` | An empty string because the split occurs at the end of the string (no characters after the final space) |

If you don’t want the trailing empty string, you can filter it out or use `re.split(r'(\s)', text, maxsplit=0)` and then drop empty entries.
